section: Mughal architecture - Fatehpur Sikri, Humayun's tomb, Taj Mahal, Red Fort; garden and tomb traditions
subsections: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)
Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin

accepted.s: Who commissioned the construction of Humayun's Tomb at Delhi?
accepted.x: Humayun's Tomb was commissioned by his widow Haji Begum, also known as Bega Begum. It was constructed during Akbar's reign.
accepted.tq: Test the precise patron rather than confusing closely related Mughal royal women.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Humayun's Tomb at Delhi was constructed approximately during which period?
accepted.x: Humayun's Tomb was built approximately between 1565 and 1572.
accepted.tq: Use the monument's construction range to distinguish it from later Mughal monuments.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following monuments is regarded as the first garden tomb in the Mughal architectural tradition?
accepted.x: Humayun's Tomb at Delhi is regarded as the first garden tomb in the Mughal architectural tradition.
accepted.tq: Directly identify the architectural distinction attached to a monument.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri — Akbar
2. Jama Masjid, Delhi — Shah Jahan
3. Moti Masjid, Agra Fort — Shah Jahan
4. Buland Darwaza — Shah Jahan
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri was built by Akbar, while the Jama Masjid of Delhi and Moti Masjid of Agra Fort were built by Shah Jahan. Buland Darwaza was built by Akbar, not Shah Jahan.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped builder in a monument–ruler pairing.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri was constructed approximately during which period?
accepted.x: Akbar constructed the Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri approximately between 1571 and 1574.
accepted.tq: Distinguish closely spaced construction periods of monuments built under Akbar.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tomb of Salim Chishti at Fatehpur Sikri is situated in the courtyard of the:
accepted.x: The Tomb of Salim Chishti is situated in the courtyard of the Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri.
accepted.tq: Test the exact architectural location within a monument complex.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Tomb of Salim Chishti — Fatehpur Sikri
accepted.x: The Taj Mahal is situated at Agra, not Delhi. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
accepted.tq: Find the wrong location among familiar monument–place pairs.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Tomb of Salim Chishti at Fatehpur Sikri was constructed approximately during:
accepted.x: The Tomb of Salim Chishti was constructed approximately in 1580–1581 during Akbar's reign.
accepted.tq: Separate the dates of monuments constructed successively at Fatehpur Sikri.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who began the construction of Akbar's Tomb, and who completed it?
o: Jahangir began it and Shah Jahan completed it
Akbar began it and Jahangir completed it
Humayun began it and Akbar completed it
Shah Jahan began it and Aurangzeb completed it
accepted.x: Akbar began the construction of his tomb, and his son Jahangir completed it. The tomb is located at Sikandra near Agra.
accepted.tq: Use the succession-based builder trap in which the initiator and completer are different rulers.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Akbar's Tomb at Sikandra was completed approximately in:
accepted.x: Akbar's Tomb at Sikandra was completed under Jahangir approximately in 1613.
accepted.tq: Match the monument with its completion date rather than its starting date.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Char Minar at Hyderabad was built by:
accepted.x: Char Minar was built at Hyderabad in 1591 by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah of the Qutb Shahi dynasty. It is not a Mughal monument.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between rulers of the Qutb Shahi dynasty and Mughal builders.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order of their construction:
A. Humayun's Tomb
B. Jami Masjid, Fatehpur Sikri
C. Tomb of Salim Chishti
D. Char Minar
accepted.x: The order is Humayun's Tomb (1565–1572), Jami Masjid at Fatehpur Sikri (1571–1574), Tomb of Salim Chishti (1580–1581), and Char Minar (1591).
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest monuments first, then compare the closely dated middle entries.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following monuments in chronological order of construction:
A. Akbar's Tomb
B. Taj Mahal
C. Red Fort, Delhi
D. Jama Masjid, Delhi
accepted.x: Akbar's Tomb was completed around 1613, followed by the Taj Mahal (1632–1648), Red Fort (1639–1648), and Jama Masjid of Delhi (1650–1656).
accepted.tq: Arrange monuments by their beginning or completion periods, paying attention to overlapping ranges.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad was built by Prince Azam Shah for:
accepted.x: Prince Azam Shah built Bibi ka Maqbara during Aurangzeb's reign for his mother, Dilras Banu Begum. It is popularly called the Taj of the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Link the monument with its patron, dedicatee and popular description.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following monuments is popularly known as the ‘Taj of the Deccan’?
accepted.x: Bibi ka Maqbara at Aurangabad is popularly known as the Taj of the Deccan.
accepted.tq: Identify the monument from its distinctive popular title.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Ram Bagh at Agra was established by Babur around 1528. Itimad-ud-Daula was built under Nur Jahan, Bibi ka Maqbara under Prince Azam Shah, and Akbar's Tomb is at Sikandra.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure monument–builder pair and eliminate reversed ruler associations.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding Mughal monuments is correct?
1. The Red Fort at Delhi was built by Shah Jahan.
2. The Red Fort was situated in Shahjahanabad.
3. The Diwan-i-Khas of the Red Fort housed the Peacock Throne.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Shah Jahan built the Red Fort at Delhi in Shahjahanabad, and its Diwan-i-Khas housed the Peacock Throne.
accepted.tq: Recognize a complete set of linked facts about builder, location and architectural function.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Red Fort at Delhi was constructed approximately during which period?
accepted.x: The Red Fort at Delhi was constructed approximately between 1639 and 1648 under Shah Jahan.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Red Fort's construction period from that of Delhi's Jama Masjid.
accepted.sec: Monument → builder and chronological order (Humayun's tomb to Char Minar)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about the Taj Mahal is correct?
1. It is the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal.
2. It was built by Shah Jahan at Agra.
3. It stands on the right bank of the Yamuna.
4. Its chief architect was Ustad Ahmad Lahori.
accepted.x: The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan at Agra as the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal, on the right bank of the Yamuna. Ustad Ahmad Lahori is identified as its chief architect.
accepted.tq: Use a multi-fact monument profile and verify each statement before selecting the combination.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal?
accepted.x: Ustad Ahmad Lahori is identified as the chief architect of the Taj Mahal.
accepted.tq: Test the specific architect associated with the monument rather than a general Mughal architect.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The design of the Taj Mahal was particularly inspired by which earlier Mughal monument?
accepted.x: Humayun's Tomb provided an important design ancestry for the Taj Mahal, particularly through the garden-tomb form and use of a double dome.
accepted.tq: Trace architectural influence from an earlier monument rather than selecting a later or contemporary structure.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following features of Humayun's Tomb contributed to its architectural influence on the Taj Mahal?
1. Garden-tomb layout
2. Double dome
3. Combination of red sandstone and marble
accepted.x: Humayun's Tomb combined a garden-tomb layout, a double dome, and red sandstone with marble. These features formed part of the architectural ancestry of the Taj Mahal.
accepted.tq: Break an architectural influence into its component features before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the position of the Taj Mahal within its charbagh?
o: The tomb stands at the southern entrance of the garden.
The tomb stands at the exact centre of the garden.
The tomb stands outside the charbagh on the western side.
The tomb stands at the river end of the charbagh.
accepted.x: Unlike the usual central placement in a charbagh, the Taj Mahal's tomb stands at the river end of the garden, near the Yamuna.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Taj Mahal's exceptional garden placement from the usual central-tomb arrangement.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the Taj Mahal is NOT correct?
o: It was built entirely of red sandstone.
It is associated with the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal.
It was built at Agra by Shah Jahan.
It represents a high point of pietra dura and symmetry.
accepted.x: The Taj Mahal is principally constructed of white marble, not entirely of red sandstone. It is the mausoleum of Mumtaz Mahal and is noted for pietra dura and symmetry.
accepted.tq: Reject the material-based reversal between the Taj Mahal and earlier red-sandstone Mughal monuments.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Taj Mahal was constructed approximately during which period, while the whole complex is sometimes dated to 1653 in older accounts?
accepted.x: The main construction period of the Taj Mahal is given as 1632–1648. Older accounts sometimes cite 1653 as the year in which the entire complex was completed.
accepted.tq: Separate the principal construction period from a later date associated with completion of the whole complex.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following features is most closely associated with the Taj Mahal's artistic significance?
accepted.x: The Taj Mahal is regarded as a high point of pietra dura decoration and architectural symmetry.
accepted.tq: Identify the defining artistic feature instead of a general architectural element.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Taj Mahal is threatened by the phenomenon popularly known as ‘marble cancer’, which is primarily associated with:
accepted.x: Sulphur dioxide emitted by the Mathura refinery, industries and traffic contributes to yellowing and the deterioration popularly called marble cancer.
accepted.tq: Apply the environmental cause to the monument affected by pollution.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Taj Trapezium Zone (TTZ) rulings concerning protection of the Taj Mahal are associated with the case of:
accepted.x: The Supreme Court's Taj Trapezium Zone rulings, including those concerning industrial pollution, were associated with the M.C. Mehta case in 1996.
accepted.tq: Match an environmental protection measure with the relevant legal case.
accepted.sec: Taj Mahal - architect, marble source, views on style origin  [APPSC]
